title: South Korea Launches 614 PFLOPS Hangang Supercomputer Ahead of May 2027 IonQ Quantum Link - Quantum Computing Report
gist: South Korea's MSIT and KISTI inaugurated Hangang, a 614 PFLOPS HPE Cray EX400 supercomputer built on 8,496 Nvidia GH200 superchips, designed as the HPC backbone for a hybrid platform linking on-site to IonQ's Tempo trapped-ion processor via Nvidia NVQLink by May 2027. It anchors the K-Moonshot program and opens for production access December 14, 2026.

insights.claim: South Korea's sixth national supercomputer, Hangang, is an HPE Cray EX400 system with a theoretical peak of 614 petaflops, a 24-fold increase over its predecessor Nurion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Confirms HPE and Nvidia as the incumbent vendors in sovereign HPC buildouts.
insights.quote: achieves a theoretical peak performance of 614 petaflops—a 24-fold increase over its predecessor, Nurion
insights.locator: South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT

insights.claim: Hangang uses 8,496 Nvidia GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips plus 9,936 CPUs, with 205 PB of storage and a network fabric above 400 Gbps.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A large single-site GH200 order shows national labs remain a material demand channel for Nvidia.

insights.claim: Hangang was procured under a total procurement and 5-year maintenance contract of about 448.3 billion won (~$336M USD).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives a reference price point for a ~600 PFLOPS national-class system including service.

insights.claim: Hangang is 100% direct liquid cooled with a PUE of 1.15, down from 1.35 on Nurion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Direct liquid cooling is becoming standard in flagship HPC, supporting liquid-cooling supply chains.

insights.claim: Nvidia's GH200 links an Arm-based Grace CPU and Hopper GPU via a 900 GB/s bidirectional interconnect, exposing a unified 576 GB address space that removes PCIe memory transfer bottlenecks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Coherent CPU-GPU memory is a key differentiator for memory-bound scientific workloads.
insights.quote: This architecture eliminates PCIe memory transfer bottlenecks by exposing a unified 576 GB address space to the operating system
insights.locator: Hangang’s core architecture leverages Nvidia’s GH200

insights.claim: In early pilot benchmarks, research teams achieved up to a 41.8x speedup over prior-generation A100 GPU clusters on memory-bound workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Large generational speedups on memory-bound jobs strengthen the upgrade case for older A100 installations.
insights.quote: research teams achieved up to a 41.8× performance speedup over prior-generation A100 GPU clusters on memory-bound workloads
insights.locator: Hangang’s core architecture leverages Nvidia’s GH200

insights.claim: Hangang will connect on-site to an IonQ Tempo trapped-ion processor (~100 physical qubits, #AQ 64) through Nvidia NVQLink and CUDA-Q, with go-live targeted for May 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A dated national deployment milestone for IonQ and validation of Nvidia's quantum-classical interconnect strategy.

insights.claim: The quantum link implements a trilateral agreement signed in March 2026 among KISTI, Nvidia, and IonQ.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Nvidia positioning itself as the integration layer between national HPC and quantum hardware vendors.
insights.quote: The system’s quantum interface realizes the trilateral agreement executed between KISTI, Nvidia, and IonQ in March 2026.

insights.claim: Tempo's trapped barium-ion architecture offers all-to-all qubit connectivity, which eliminates SWAP-gate routing overheads when mapping non-local Hamiltonian terms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Connectivity is a selling point for trapped-ion over fixed-lattice modalities in chemistry workloads.
insights.quote: Tempo’s trapped barium-ion architecture provides all-to-all qubit connectivity, eliminating routing SWAP gate overheads

insights.claim: The hybrid design assigns classical data preparation, parameter updates and post-processing to GH200 nodes, while offloading structured subroutines such as molecular ground-state and combinatorial optimization phases to the quantum processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Illustrates that near-term quantum value is framed as an accelerator inside classical HPC, not standalone.

insights.claim: Hangang anchors South Korea's K-Moonshot initiative, backed by 10.1 trillion won (~$7.5 billion USD) in 2026 AI R&D funding across 12 national challenges including battery materials, clean energy and quantum computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Large state AI R&D budgets create sustained sovereign demand for compute and quantum pilots.
insights.locator: Hangang anchors the South Korean government’s

insights.claim: Hangang capacity is allocated 55% to general research, 30% to national strategic R&D (K-Moonshot), and 15% to SMEs and startups.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Subsidized compute for startups may seed a domestic Korean AI and quantum software ecosystem.

insights.claim: After pilot trials serving about 190 projects, Hangang opens for full production access on December 14, 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Near-term operational date for Korean research and commercial users.
